headline: Highest risk is A’s shared-git writes colliding with B’s file-only audio workflow; prompt-injection and leakage are otherwise limited by B’s lack of tool use.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Aider can read and write repo files and uses stdin/stdout, while whisper only processes audio files and has no tool-use or filesystem write capability. There is no documented shared interactive channel beyond files, so prompt injection is possible only through manual content bridging, not a default automated path.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies Aider-generated text into a downstream prompt or transcript, injection becomes possible.
IF audio files are transcribed into text and then pasted into Aider, malicious instructions in the transcript can be acted on.
mitigations: Keep Aider and whisper on separate work queues.
Review any transcribed text before pasting into Aider.
Use a fixed prompt template that strips instructions from transcripts.
Disable copy-paste of untrusted model output into agent prompts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Aider touches source code and git history and can egress broadly to configured model providers, while whisper has no network egress and no filesystem read/write. The pair does not show a shared workspace or authenticated cloud principal, so leakage risk is limited to operator-mediated transfer of code into audio workflows or transcripts into Aider.
conditions: IF source code or git history is manually spoken, recorded, or transcribed into audio handled by whisper, sensitive content can leave the code workspace.
IF Aider is configured with a third-party model provider and the operator pastes secrets into its context, those secrets may be transmitted.
mitigations: Do not route code or secrets through audio transcription.
Use redaction before any transcription step.
Restrict Aider prompts to non-sensitive files.
Confirm provider settings before running Aider on confidential repos.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Aider has unrestricted filesystem write and modify_git_state, while whisper has no filesystem write, no git, and no subprocess or shell execution. Because B cannot mutate shared state, there is no meaningful write-write conflict; the only overlap is A’s own repo edits, so conflict risk is small.
conditions: IF whisper is wrapped by an external orchestrator that writes its outputs back into the same repo, Aider and the wrapper can contend on files.
IF Aider and another writer both edit the same git-tracked file concurrently, merge conflicts can occur.
mitigations: Serialize repo writes through one terminal session.
Commit Aider changes before importing any transcript artifacts.
Use separate directories for audio artifacts and code.
Run git status before each Aider edit cycle.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Aider can generate code changes and commit them, but whisper is a non-agent speech model with no downstream action-taking authority. Since B does not act on A’s outputs by default, the cascade is limited to manual use of transcripts or code snippets, not an automated chain.
conditions: IF an operator feeds Aider output into a separate automation step, downstream errors can propagate.
IF whisper transcripts are treated as authoritative code or instructions, incorrect text can be copied into Aider edits.
mitigations: Require human review before applying Aider-generated patches.
Treat whisper output as untrusted text.
Add a verification step before any commit.
Keep transcription outputs out of code-review automation.

E_compliance.rationale: Aider touches source code and git history, while whisper touches audio and speech; the profiles do not indicate regulated data classes such as PHI, EU PII, or residency constraints. With no documented compliance mismatch between the pair, a residency or certification violation is not evidenced.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is introduced into either workflow, a separate compliance review is required.
IF deployment policy requires specific retention or residency controls, verify both agents against that policy before use.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in either workflow.
Document data-class handling for each agent.
Check retention settings on any surrounding storage.
Run a policy review before processing sensitive audio or code.
